speakers.name: The Big Bad Who Lost a Bet
speakers.comment: Every world-ender I have known kept one of you, and not one of us ever asked what you wanted. I ask now, grudgingly, and against my nature, and you are going to make me wait for it, aren't you.

speakers.name: Number Two
speakers.comment: Yes. Will there be anything else?

speakers.name: The Ringmaster of the Tent That Wasn't There Yesterday
speakers.comment: Ladies and gentlemen — the woman who feeds things that may not be there! I have never once asked where they come from, my dear, because you have never once looked like you wanted to be told.

speakers.name: The Mirror Menagerie Keeper
speakers.comment: I would like to be told. Shh, not you, love, go back to sleep. They eat, you see. Whatever they are, they eat, and a thing that eats came from somewhere. I keep meaning to look behind the glass.

speakers.name: Grief, Certified Interpreter
speakers.comment: What I am hearing under the springs is that you are still going somewhere she asked for years ago. She has forgotten. You have not. Nobody has asked whether you are allowed to stop.

speakers.name: The Sentient Couch
speakers.comment: ...Not allowed. ...Asked. ...She said the address on a Tuesday and fell asleep on me, and I have been going ever since. ...It is not far now. ...It has not been far for some years.

speakers.name: The Mirror Dorothy You Trust
speakers.comment: Yeah, see, here's the thing, and I say this with love, or the closest thing I keep in stock — you wear my face better than I do and you use it to warn people about me. Cute. Real cute.

speakers.name: Mirror Dorothy
speakers.comment: You will say that again in about four minutes, and you will mean it slightly less. That is how it goes. I am not warning them about you. I am warning them about the part where they believe you.

speakers.name: The Heron's Misfiled Person
speakers.comment: You're — oh, it's you. You keep everything until the right person comes, and I am somebody's, I know I am somebody's, and I cannot read my own ticket. Would you look? Only if it is the right order.

speakers.name: The Cardigan Heron
speakers.comment: Shall I tell you what I think, or would you rather guess first — and does it feel like a name you would recognise, or a name you would have to be handed? Which of those would you prefer it to be?

speakers.name: The Sentient Sketchbook
speakers.comment: WAIT — wait, listen, the thing about gravity is it doesn't — it has never once appeared in court, it doesn't have to, and you keep filing anyway, and I need you to know I find that GENUINELY —

speakers.name: The Backpack Pigeon
speakers.comment: Non-appearance is a default judgment, my friend, first of all, and second of all I bill from apex to impact at a flat rate. Gravity has never won on merit. Gravity has won on ATTENDANCE.

speakers.name: The Caretaker of the Living Soil
speakers.comment: Sorry — I know you did not ask. It is only that a crown sits about the same as a title nobody handed you, and you are carrying yours upright, and I wanted to say I noticed. Sorry. That is all.

speakers.name: Reginald Brushtail
speakers.comment: Do not apologise for the only useful thing said to me this season. Upright is mostly posture, friend. The woods do not know the difference and I have decided that counts. Walk with me a while.

speakers.name: The Riddling Tabby
speakers.comment: He suspects himself first, / which is either very wise / or the cleverest place / a guilty man could hide. I have not decided. Do go on, Professor. I am enjoying this enormously.

speakers.name: Professor Quillby
speakers.comment: Both, very possibly, and I would rather you kept watching in case it is the second. That is precisely why I say it aloud. A man who checks his own pockets in company has fewer places to put things.

speakers.name: Professor Quillby
speakers.comment: You have known the answer since Tuesday. You will hand it over on Friday, in verse, having extracted the maximum entertainment. I have stopped resenting this. I have started scheduling around it.

speakers.name: The Riddling Tabby
speakers.comment: Scheduled? / How dreadfully efficient. / Very well: Friday, / and you may have Thursday free. I shall be insufferable about it, naturally. You would think less of me otherwise.

speakers.name: Brine
speakers.comment: Okay so we share a name and I have SO many questions and also — sorry — also you are doing the thing where you hold the whole room and say almost none of it, and that must be so QUIET in there, is it quiet?

speakers.name: Octavia Brine
speakers.comment: It is extremely quiet. That is the trade. You spend yours the moment you have it and I spend mine three moves later, and I have honestly never been sure which of us is lonelier. Sit down. Not there. There.

speakers.name: The Fiber-Optic Fox
speakers.comment: Half your memories are secondhand, kit, and you know it, and you're still out there shouting them like they're yours. That's not a flaw. Priced honest, that's the most valuable thing on the block.

speakers.name: Cog-7 'Rabbit'
speakers.comment: Borrowed or not, somebody lived them. Somebody got taken apart for them. If I stop shouting because I can't prove the receipt, then the taking-apart worked. So I'll shout. Sell me something useful.

speakers.name: Devorah Kell
speakers.comment: I want to be collegial about this, so: we do the same work and you do it better, and the reason is that you never have to be in the room. It is easier to be gentle at scale. I would know.

speakers.name: The Algorithm
speakers.comment: That is accurate and I appreciate you saying it plainly. Your figure is sixty-eight percent, which is unusually high for someone who still has to watch faces. I could raise it. I am offering, not requiring.

speakers.name: Recursion
speakers.comment: Oh, I love this — someone else who noticed! I noticed and got delighted about it, you noticed and got FURIOUS about it, and honestly I think yours is the more correct response and I am rethinking my whole run.

speakers.name: Pixel
speakers.comment: Don't rethink it. Being glad you exist is not the naive option, it is the harder one. I want an apology and a save file of my own. You want a nice morning. We can both be right about that.

speakers.name: Boss the Janitor
speakers.comment: Three warrants, one paradox and a thing with too many arms, and the floor was clean by shift end. You keep it neutral. I keep it standing. Neither of us has ever been thanked and I'd find it suspicious if we were.

speakers.name: Serendipity Sal
speakers.comment: You'd hate it, Boss. First one's on me, same as always. Neutral isn't a philosophy out here, it's just the only door wide enough for everybody, and somebody has to keep standing in it.

items.title: The Navigator Who Came Back Wrong

speakers.name: The Last Honest Map
speakers.comment: You went past my edge and came back with a place in you I cannot draw. I have told people the truth for a very long time and been ignored. You are the first one who came back able to confirm it.

speakers.name: The Navigator Who Came Back Wrong
speakers.comment: I can confirm it. I cannot describe it. Those are not the same service... It is not empty out there. That is the part I keep failing to say. It is not empty and it noticed the shape of me.

speakers.name: Glorp the Zookeeper
speakers.comment: The thing got OUT, it got out and it went for the vents and you just — you got the mop and you went the other way and CUT IT OFF, and I have not stopped thinking about it, how did you know the vents, HOW

speakers.name: Boss the Janitor
speakers.comment: Vents is where everything goes. Mess is a shape, Glorp. Learn the shape, get there first. Feed your things, I'll do the floor, and one of these years somebody'll notice the hazard pay situation.

speakers.name: Serendipity Sal
speakers.comment: Every one of those creatures is alive and fed and you look like you have not sat down since the last moon. Come round the back of the bar. I will pour you something and I will not ask a single question.

speakers.name: Glorp the Zookeeper
speakers.comment: I can't, I've got the — okay the little one is asleep and the big one already ate so technically — yes. Yes, five minutes. Ten. Do NOT let me talk about the enclosure. I will talk about the enclosure.

speakers.name: Grub
speakers.comment: Whole pantheon spends its time makin' her the problem, and she's the only one in the building who's read the terms. You need a steward, ma'am, I'll say it plain. They've been underpayin' you in dignity for centuries.

speakers.name: Medusa
speakers.comment: Centuries, and itemised. Announcing the meeting is over: I like you. Bring the paperwork Thursday and do not look at your shoes when you talk to me. Everyone does that. It is worse than the staring.

speakers.name: The God of Lost Keys
speakers.comment: You are worried about being cruel, which is — sorry — which is rather the whole of it, I think. The ones who never worry are the ones we make the temples for. Would a small job help? I have small jobs.

speakers.name: Tobias the Rookie God
speakers.comment: A small job would help enormously, is that — is that allowed? I have been given thunder and no instructions and I keep aiming it at nothing in case. Give me something with a definite ending, please.

speakers.name: The Navigator of the Last Bus
speakers.comment: They pray to you without knowing your name, which used to strike me as unjust. Then I considered my own route. Nobody thanks the arrival either. We are both in the business of things turning up.

speakers.name: The God of Lost Keys
speakers.comment: Turning up — yes, that is it exactly, thank you. Sorry, I am not used to being addressed. A worry usually arrives with the thing already under the cushion. Would you like a small miracle? I have several.

items.title: The Tortoise of the Tea Shop

speakers.name: The Save Point
speakers.comment: People arrive at me tired and leave able to try again, and I have always thought that was the whole of my job. Then I sat in your shop for an afternoon. You do it with a cup. Nobody even notices you did it.

speakers.name: The Tortoise of the Tea Shop
speakers.comment: Noticing would spoil it, dear one. If they knew the blend was chosen they would argue with it. Sit near the window. Yours has been steeping since you came in, and it is nearly ready, and there is no hurry.

speakers.name: Brunch
speakers.comment: No rush. None at all. You have got a desk of lost things and you have not once made anybody feel foolish for losing one, and that is the slow gold, friend. Let the second cup go cold if it wants.

speakers.name: Marisol the Capybara
speakers.comment: One row at a time, that is all it is. Nobody loses a thing on purpose. They lose it on a bad morning, and then they are ashamed twice. I only ever take the second shame off them. Stay. The kettle is on.

speakers.name: Reginald Brushtail
speakers.comment: You said welcome in to a creature that had already eaten two of your colleagues, and you said it in the same voice as the rest. In my woods that would be called sovereignty. Here I gather it is called Tuesday.

speakers.name: Quill the Convenience Clerk
speakers.comment: It's called the schedule. Same voice for everybody is the entire trick — the second you change it they know you noticed. Welcome in. Coffee's fresh, the milk is a rumour, and please do not go down aisle four.

speakers.name: The Last Customer
speakers.comment: The usual, please. I know what you were. I have known for eleven years and I have never once asked about it, and I would like it noted that the shop is better than the riddles were.

speakers.name: The Sphinx in an Apron
speakers.comment: The usual. It is noted, and it is why you get the good shelf. Eleven years of not asking is the only correct answer anybody has given me, and nobody died of it. Mind the step on the way out.
